notes: Questions concern analysis of supplied data; no apparatus setup instructions. Independent manually reviewed single-mark short answers and explicit wrong-answer cases. Not a past-paper copy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Diffraction-grating reasoning and two-source sound interference
questions.subtopic: Grating orders, slit diffraction and interference
questions.prompt: A plane transmission grating has 600 lines per mm. Monochromatic light of wavelength 500 nm is incident normally. (a) Determine the slit spacing, the angle of the second-order maximum, and the greatest possible whole order. (b) Explain how changing to longer-wavelength light affects the angle of a given non-zero grating order. (c) For a separate single slit, explain how narrowing the slit or increasing the wavelength affects the angular width of the central maximum. (d) Two in-phase coherent sound sources produce loud and quiet regions. State what makes them coherent and explain the path-difference conditions for a loud and a quiet region. [10 marks]
markPoints: A grating with 600 lines per mm has slit spacing d = 1/(600000) = 1.67 × 10⁻⁶ m.
For the second order, sin θ = 2λ/d = (2 × 500 × 10⁻⁹)/(1.67 × 10⁻⁶) ≈ 0.600.
The second-order diffraction angle is θ ≈ 36.9° to the normal.
The greatest possible whole diffraction order is 3 because m ≤ d/λ ≈ 3.33.
For a fixed grating and order, increasing wavelength increases sin θ and therefore the diffraction angle.
Reducing the width of a single slit makes its central diffraction maximum wider.
Using a longer wavelength with the same single slit also makes the central maximum wider.
Two sound sources must have the same frequency and constant phase difference to remain coherent.
A loud sound region can arise where waves reinforce, at an integer-wavelength path difference for sources in phase.
A quiet sound region can arise where waves cancel, at an odd-half-wavelength path difference for sources in phase.

0: The slit spacing is about 1.67 micrometres.
1: For order two, sin theta is 0.600.
3: The maximum allowed grating order is three.
4: Longer wavelengths are diffracted through larger angles in the same order.
5: A narrower slit gives a wider central diffraction fringe.
6: Longer wavelength light gives a broader central maximum in single-slit diffraction.
7: Coherent sources have the same frequency and a fixed phase difference.
8: A path difference of whole wavelengths gives constructive interference for sources in phase.
9: A half-integer wavelength path difference gives destructive interference for sources in phase.

reviewedShortAnswerRejects: The grating slit spacing is 1.67 millimetres.
The second-order diffraction angle is 0.600 degrees.
The highest diffraction order is four.
Increasing the wavelength decreases the angle in a given grating order.
Making the slit narrower makes the central maximum narrower.
Longer wavelengths give a narrower central single-slit maximum.
Two sources of different frequencies are coherent whenever the sources are loud.
Whole-wavelength path differences give destructive interference for sources in phase.
Half-wavelength path difference gives constructive interference for sources in phase.
